note: PLACEHOLDER. Every params object here validates against the published meeting_schedule manifest input_schema (additionalProperties: false, $refs inlined the way publish_experiments.py inlines them), and every value is plausible, but nobody has dispatched one. So a verdict drawn from this list is a claim about the pipeline, not about the agent. EIGHT cases, and DEFAULT_JUDGE_CONFIG.gates.minCases is 20. A corpus verdict over this list therefore resolves CAN'T SAY however the judge voted, because the floor was set from measured agent non-determinism and eight runs measure that rather than the branch. Eight is deliberate and not a rounding error: one clean baseline plus seven single-axis variations is what one change can author honestly across nine agents. Whether to grow every list to 20 or to lower the floor is still open — do not read the shortfall as a decision. Varied along: how much of the jurisdiction the office string carries, which is the whole difficulty of this agent — 'Burnsville City Council Member' names its city, 'Center Township Trustee' names one that exists in dozens of Indiana counties, and a bare 'City Council' names none, forcing inference from position plus state; whether a location hint from a prior run is supplied; whether the opaque elected_office_id passthrough is present; city council against mayor against county commission against school board against township; and a large city that publishes an annual meeting calendar against a small jurisdiction whose schedule lives in a municipal-code section. People are fictional placeholders in the house style (gp-webapp e2e-tests briefings.spec.ts uses 'Test Official'); this file is public, so no real person is named. States, cities, office titles and L2 voter file column names are real.
